pumac-2013-geometry-a-01.title: Area as a sum of three triangles
pumac-2013-geometry-a-01.body:
$[ABC]=[OAB]+[OBC]+[OCA]$ (as $O$ lies inside $ABC$, the three angles being $120^\circ$), and $[OAB]=\frac12\cdot OA\cdot OB\sin120^\circ=\frac{\sqrt3}4\,OA\cdot OB$. So $[ABC]=\frac{\sqrt3}4(ab+bc+ca)$ with $a=OA$, etc.

The lengths $a,b,c$ are independent and uniformly distributed on $\{3,4,5\}$ (mean $4$), so $E[ab]=16$, and the average area is $\frac{\sqrt3}4\cdot3\cdot16=12\sqrt3$. Hence $m+n=12+3=15$.

**Answer: 15**

pumac-2013-geometry-a-03.title: Two stages of the roll
pumac-2013-geometry-a-03.body:
The shape is a circular sector with center $A$, radius $6$ and angle $60^\circ$.

**Stage 1: rolling on the arc.** The sector rolls like a wheel of radius $6$ on its arc until $C$ touches $l$. The arc $BC$ has length $6\cdot\frac\pi3=2\pi$, so the center $A$ moves horizontally by $2\pi$ at height $6$. The region swept is the rectangle of width $2\pi$ and height $6$, of area $12\pi$.

**Stage 2: pivoting about $C$.** Now $AC$ is vertical. The sector rotates about $C$ by $90^\circ$ until $A$ reaches the line. The farthest points of the sector from $C$ are $A$ and $B$ at distance $6$, so the sector sweeps a quarter disc of radius $6$ centered at $C$, of area $\frac14\pi\cdot36=9\pi$, to the right of the rectangle.

The total area is $12\pi+9\pi=21\pi$, so $n=21$.

**Answer: 21**

pumac-2013-geometry-a-06.title: Orthocenter vectors
pumac-2013-geometry-a-06.body:
Take the circumcenter as the origin. The orthocenter of a triangle inscribed in the circle is the sum of its vertex vectors, so $H=A+B+C$, $I=B+C+D$, $J=C+D+A$, $K=D+A+B$. Then
$$I-H=D-A,\quad J-I=A-B,\quad K-J=B-C,\quad H-K=C-D.$$
Hence $AD=2$, $AB=3$, $BC=4$, $CD=5$.

For a cyclic quadrilateral with sides $AB=a$, $BC=b$, $CD=c$, $DA=d$, Ptolemy ($AC\cdot BD=ac+bd$) together with $\frac{AC}{BD}=\frac{ad+bc}{ab+cd}$ gives
$$BD^2=\frac{(ac+bd)(ab+cd)}{ad+bc}=\frac{(15+8)(12+10)}{6+20}=\frac{23\cdot22}{26}=\frac{253}{13}.$$
So $13\,BD^2=253$.

**Answer: 253**

pumac-2013-geometry-a-07.title: Isosceles trapezoid
pumac-2013-geometry-a-07.body:
$\angle BAC=18^\circ+30^\circ=48^\circ=\angle ACP$. Draw the line through $P$ parallel to $AC$ and let it meet $AB$ at $Q$. Then $ACPQ$ is a trapezoid with equal base angles at $A$ and $C$ ($\angle QAC=\angle ACP=48^\circ$), so it is an isosceles trapezoid and its diagonals are equal: $CQ=AP=BC$. Also $\angle QCA=\angle PAC=30^\circ$ by symmetry.

In triangle $AQC$: $\angle AQC=180^\circ-48^\circ-30^\circ=102^\circ$, so $\angle BQC=78^\circ$. Triangle $CQB$ is isosceles with $CQ=CB$, so $\angle ABC=\angle CBQ=\angle BQC=78^\circ$. Then $\angle ACB=180^\circ-48^\circ-78^\circ=54^\circ$ and $\angle BCP=54^\circ-48^\circ=6^\circ$.

**Answer: 6**

pumac-2013-geometry-a-07.title: Coordinate check
pumac-2013-geometry-a-07.body:
Put $A$ at the origin, $AB$ along the $x$-axis, $AC=1$ at angle $48^\circ$, $P$ on the ray at $18^\circ$ with $\angle ACP=48^\circ$ (so $AP=\frac{\sin48^\circ}{\sin102^\circ}$) and $B$ on the $x$-axis with $BC=AP$. Computing $\angle BCP$ numerically gives $6^\circ$ (the other intersection gives a configuration with $P$ outside the triangle).

**Answer: 6**

pumac-2013-geometry-a-08.title: Coordinates along the three chords
pumac-2013-geometry-a-08.body:
Put the common point $X$ at the origin and the chords along the coordinate axes. Let the sphere have center $O=(o_1,o_2,o_3)$ and radius $R$. Along the $i$-th axis, the endpoints of the chord are the roots of $t^2-2o_it+(|O|^2-R^2)=0$. Their product is $|O|^2-R^2=-p$ where $p=R^2-|O|^2>0$ (the point $X$ is inside), and their difference is the chord length $l_i$, so
$$l_i^2=4o_i^2+4p\ \Rightarrow\ o_i^2=\frac{l_i^2}4-p.$$
Then $R^2=|O|^2+p=\sum\frac{l_i^2}4-3p+p=\frac{25+36+49}4-2p=\frac{55}2-2p$.

Since $o_i^2\ge0$ for all $i$, $p\le\min\frac{l_i^2}4=\frac{25}4$. So $R^2\ge\frac{55}2-\frac{25}2=15$, with equality when $p=\frac{25}4$ (then $o_1=0$, $o_2^2=\frac{11}4$, $o_3^2=6$, all valid).

**Answer: 15**
